title: abies religiosa subsp. perotensis
intro: Abies religiosa subsp. perotensis, commonly known as Mexican fir or Perot's fir, is a subspecies of evergreen tree native to Mexico and parts of Central America, characterized by its distinctive needle-like leaves and conical shape. The wood and extracts of Mexican fir have been used in traditional medicine to treat various health issues, including fever, inflammation, and respiratory problems, due to its numerous health benefits such as antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antiseptic properties. The therapeutic actions of Mexican fir include its ability to reduce fever, alleviate pain, and soothe respiratory issues, making it a valuable remedy in traditional medicine. The bioactive constituents of Mexican fir include terpenes, flavonoids, and phenolic compounds, which contribute to its medicinal properties and make it a valuable resource for natural remedies.
